jurisdiction.name: Israel
jurisdiction.overview: Israel governs AI through a sectoral, soft-law 'responsible innovation' approach with no AI-specific statute; national AI strategy is now led from the Prime Minister's Office.

narrative.summary: Israel has no AI-specific law. Its 2023 Principles of Policy, Regulation and Ethics in AI, issued by the Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology and the Ministry of Justice, set a 'responsible innovation' model: each regulator acts in its own sector with soft, risk-based tools aligned to international standards, guided by national AI ethics principles. Strategy moved from the TELEM-designed National AI Program (Government Resolution 212 of 2021) to a National AI Directorate in the Prime Minister's Office. The Directorate was set up after the 2025 Nagel Committee report and published the August 2026 National AI Strategic Plan under Government Resolution 4255. Binding obligations come mainly from the Privacy Protection Law, strengthened by Amendment 13 (in force August 2025). The Privacy Protection Authority has issued a draft guideline on applying that law to AI (2025) and guidance on AI agents (2026). Sector regulators are the most active layer: the Bank of Israel's Directive 369 brings AI models under model-risk rules, an inter-ministerial team issued a final report on AI in finance (December 2025), the Ministry of Education regulates generative AI in schools, and the Innovation Authority and Ministry of Health run an AI health sandbox. Inside government, the National Digital Agency's guide on responsible AI use (version 1.0, May 2026) sets risk-tiered approval tracks for public bodies.
lead_institutions: National Artificial Intelligence Directorate, Prime Minister's Office
Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology (MOST)
Ministry of Justice – Office of Legal Counsel and Legislative Affairs
Bank of Israel – Banking Supervision Department
narrative.review_notes: The deep review completed on 6 October 2026 read in full the documents published as files on the government portal; some government web pages, the Knesset legislation database, the Innovation Authority and the Bank of Israel were unavailable, so four government resolutions from 2023 to 2026 are pending until their official pages are confirmed. Professional, academic and research papers were not recorded, no Israeli adoption of ISO/IEC AI standards and no AI procurement rules were found, and Israel's signature of the Council of Europe AI Convention is to be recorded in the regional section.

instruments.summary: Final government policy paper (124 pp.) setting Israel's 'responsible innovation' approach: AI regulation should be sectoral rather than horizontal, soft and incremental, risk-based and aligned with emerging international standards. It sets out national AI ethics principles (human-centricity, equality and non-discrimination, transparency and explainability, reliability, safety and security, accountability, privacy) and recommends a government AI knowledge-and-coordination centre and experimentation tools such as sandboxes. It guides regulators; it is not binding and the minister's foreword says a government resolution adopting it is still to be sought.

instruments.current_status: In force. Source is the PPA's unofficial English translation 'Updated After Amendment 13'. Amendment 13 dates from the PPA's official guide to Amendment 13 (May 2025).
instruments.summary: Israel's general data protection law, which governs the collection and processing of personal data in databases, including for AI training and use. Amendment No. 13 (passed 5 August 2024, in force 14 August 2025) updated core definitions, required data protection officers in public bodies and many companies, replaced most database registration with notification and gave the Privacy Protection Authority inspection, administrative-fine and enforcement powers. The PPA relies on it for its AI guidance.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Israel were searched, including the government portal, the Knesset, ministries and regulators. No AI procurement rules, national adoption of international AI standards or cyber-security AI document with an official text was found (a cyber advisory is listed under Leads), and Israel's signature of the Council of Europe AI Convention and the UNESCO Recommendation are shown in the regional files. Some government web pages, the Knesset database and the Innovation Authority were unavailable, so several government resolutions and issuing dates remain to be confirmed.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): Deep review completed on 6 October 2026. Documents published as files on the government portal were read in full; several government web pages, the Knesset legislation database, the Innovation Authority and the Bank of Israel's web pages could not be read automatically. Four government resolutions from 2023 to 2026 are pending until their official pages can be confirmed. Professional, academic and research papers were not recorded. No Israeli adoption of the ISO/IEC AI standards and no AI procurement rules were found. Israel's signature of the Council of Europe AI Convention is to be recorded in the regional layer.

Coverage note (original): Procurement: no AI procurement rules or model clauses found. Cyber-security: no INCD AI document with official full text found (advisory held as lead). Standards: no national adoption of ISO/IEC 42001/5339 found. International: CoE CETS 225 (signed by Israel) and the UNESCO Recommendation are held in regional files, not in the country file. Technical review notes: Deep review 2026-10-06. The existing record with title '-' was fixed in place as the December 2023 MOST/MoJ policy principles (id kept). gov.il BlobFolder PDFs could be downloaded with a browser user-agent and were read; gov.il HTML pages (government resolutions, press pages), innovationisrael.org.il (curl), boi.org.il HTML, coe.int and fs.knesset.gov.il (Knesset bills and Reshumot) returned Cloudflare/403 or challenge pages to automated reading. Government Resolutions 3375 (2025), 4255 (2026), 3574 (2025) and 173 (2023) are held as leads because their gov.il pages could not be read or their URLs confirmed. Not recorded: the Israel Bar Association ethics opinion on AI (professional body, not government), the 2022 Tel Aviv University study for the MoJ (academic), Knesset Research and Information Center papers (research, not policy), and the State Comptroller's 2026 parallel audit (to add on a later pass). Standards: the Standards Institution of Israel offers ISO/IEC 42001 certification but no Israeli standard adopting ISO/IEC 42001 or 5339 was found. Procurement: no AI-specific procurement rules found. Cyber: no INCD AI document with an official full text was located (advisory held as a lead). International: Israel signed the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS 225); this is held in data/regional/COE.json, and the PPA draft guidance (April 2025) states that Israel signed it. Unitary state: no subnational pass needed, and no official municipal AI instruments were found. Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 3 record(s) added. Ministries: Ministry of Education (schools): 20 January 2025 AI-tools guidelines, superseded by the recorded January 2026 version (recorded as historical); Council for Higher Education: nothing found (only institution-level rules); Ministry of Health: principles for AI interventional clinical trials v2.0, February 2026 (recorded; promotes existing lead); GMLP machine-learning principles found but undated (lead); Ministry of Justice: commissioned 2022 financial-sector AI report (lead, not ministry position); no ministry AI guidance for prosecutors found; Courts Administration: AI ethics procedure 01-26 still not online (existing lead kept); Israel Bar Association 2024 AI opinion (lead, not a ministry); Ministry of Defense / IDF: nothing found (only an R&D request for information); Ministry of Finance and Israel Tax Authority: nothing found beyond internal AI-use plans; Ministry of Interior, Population Authority, Israel Police: nothing found; Ministry of Foreign Affairs: nothing found; Ministry of Labor and Ministry of Welfare and Social Affairs, National Insurance Institute: nothing found (AI-and-employment measures sit in a government resolution, already a lead); Ministry of Agriculture: nothing found; Ministry of Transport and Road Safety: only a project page on using AI for planning (not an instrument); Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure: nothing found; Ministry of Environmental Protection: nothing found; Ministry of Economy and Industry: nothing found; Ministry of Communications: nothing found; Ministry of Culture and Sport: nothing found; Ministry of Tourism: AI in the Tourism Sector policy paper, April 2026 (recorded); Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology: National Priority Areas AI report, April 2025 (lead); Civil Service Commission: only an AI training course, no guidance (public-sector guide already recorded under the National Digital Agency).. Not reached: none. Could not verify: gov.il HTML pages (e.g. the Health ministry pages for the clinical-trials and GMLP documents) return 403/202 to curl and WebFetch, so issuing-page dates could not be read; PDFs on gov.il BlobFolder download normally.; Earlier December 2024 consultation version of the Ministry of Health clinical-trials principles not located on an official site..
